title: Microsoft Purview: send Microsoft Foundry prompts and responses to Purview per Azure subscription
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, controls, licensing and user-context requirements are supported. Narrow the wording about interactions staying outside Purview to the native subscription integration, because Microsoft also documents direct API integration.

claims.claim: Microsoft Foundry is Microsoft's platform for building AI applications and agents.
claims.quote: Microsoft Foundry is a developer platform that lets you embed AI models, agents, evaluation tools, and Responsible AI capabilities into your workflows and applications.

claims.claim: Foundry administrators can activate Purview per Azure subscription for centralised compliance, governance and posture management.
claims.quote: Purview enablement in AI Foundry, allows Foundry admins to activate Microsoft Purview on their subscription.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes interaction data from all apps and agents flowing into Purview once enabled.
claims.quote: Once enabled, AI interaction data from all apps and agents flows into Purview for centralized compliance, governance, and posture management of AI data.

claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/ai-m365-copilot to sources for the comparison with Microsoft 365 Copilot. Its capabilities sections cover these controls; audit is also supported by the already cited audit-copilot page.

claims.where: Why it matters: until enabled; Governance controls: at all; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Until an administrator enables one of these switches, Foundry interactions stay outside Purview.
claims.quote: Before Microsoft Purview can manage these AI interactions, ensure you perform either of the following configuration steps:
claims.fix: Narrow this to the native integration. Replace the Why it matters sentence with 'The native subscription integration requires administrator enablement.' Replace 'decide whether a subscription's interactions reach Purview at all' with 'enable the native subscription-level integration' and the rationale clause 'left off, Foundry interactions stay outside Purview' with 'left off, this native integration does not send Foundry interactions to Purview'. The cited page supports the enablement requirement, but https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/developer/secure-ai-with-purview also documents Microsoft Graph APIs and Agent Framework as alternative integration routes.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: Data security policies apply to Entra ID API calls with a user-context token or API calls explicitly including user context.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview Data Security Policies for Foundry Services interactions apply to API calls that use Microsoft Entra ID authentication with a user-context token, or for API calls that explicitly include user context.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Other authentication scenarios appear only in Audit and DSPM for AI Activity Explorer rather than receiving these data security policies.
claims.quote: For all other authentication scenarios, user interactions are displayed in Microsoft Purview Audit and AI Interactions with classifications in DSPM for AI Activity Explorer only.

claims.claim: The Purview Foundry page states that AI app prompts and responses are stored in a user's mailbox.
claims.quote: Because user prompts and responses for AI apps are stored in a user's mailbox, you can create a case and use search when a user's mailbox is selected as the source for a search query.

claims.claim: Mailbox-stored Foundry interactions can be searched with eDiscovery.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Purview portal, navigate to **eDiscovery** > **Cases** > **Create case**. In the case, create a search

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Why it matters
claims.claim: Retention policies can retain or delete Foundry AI app prompts and responses.
claims.quote: Use retention policies to automatically retain or delete user prompts and responses for AI apps.

claims.claim: Displaying prompt and response content in DSPM for AI activity explorer requires Content Explorer Content Viewer membership.
claims.quote: Drill down to each activity to view details that include displaying the prompts and response when you're a member of the Microsoft Purview Content Explorer Content Viewer role group.

claims.quote: For prompts and responses, requires a collection policy such as **DSPM for AI - Detect sensitive info shared with AI via network**

claims.claim: The Foundry page limits current DLP support to blocking prompts by sensitive information types, scoped to an Entra-registered AI app.
claims.quote: Support today is only available for a DLP policy that blocks prompts based on sensitive information types. This requires the configuration of a PowerShell cmdlet that's scoped to a specific Entra-registered AI app.

claims.claim: The Foundry Compliance documentation warns that audit visibility does not establish policy enforcement.
claims.quote: Don't equate audit visibility with data security policy enforcement.

claims.claim: Managing policies for Foundry interactions requires Purview pay-as-you-go billing, supporting variable cost.

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed, combining Purview licensing with pay-as-you-go policy features.
claims.quote: The pay-as-you-go billing model builds on the per-user licensing model. The two are complementary, not mutually exclusive.

claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell. ... This cmdlet is currently available in Public Preview, isn't available in all organizations, and is subject to change.

claims.claim: The one-click policy is named DSPM for AI - Capture interactions for enterprise AI apps.
claims.quote: **DSPM for AI - Capture interactions for enterprise AI apps** from the recommendation or remediation action **Secure interactions from enterprise apps**
